Insights & Risk Assessment

Full-period analysis · independent of the date filter · follows the department selector
How these numbers are put together
  • Risk score — each employee is scored 0–100 from four daily habits: how often they are late, leave early, miss one punch, or are absent without approved leave. The worse the habit, the higher the score. Everyone is then split at the school’s own 70% / 85% lines into Low / Medium / High — so the grades always compare staff against the rest of the school.
  • Short histories are downgraded — anyone with fewer than 5 working days is dropped one grade, because a few days are simply too little to judge a habit.
  • Punch-pattern clusters — staff are grouped into 4 types by when they usually clock in / clock out and how steady those times are (Early starters → On time → Slightly late → Late arrivals). It is a quick way to see the school’s usual rhythm.
  • Weekday effect — the share of records that were late or unexplained-absent on each weekday, so you can see whether Mondays or Fridays behave differently.
  • Weekly trend & outlook — attendance rate for each week, extended one week ahead with a simple straight line. It is an indication of direction, not a promise.
  • Unusual clock-in / clock-out days — a day is flagged when the punch falls far outside that employee’s own normal range (roughly 45+ minutes, adjusted per person). This catches genuinely odd days instead of different-but-normal ones.
Notes: insights cover the whole filtered period — weekends, public holidays and school-break days are not counted — and they follow the department you select (and the access scope of your password). The date-range filter at the top does not change them. Late / early minutes use the machine’s own values (15-minute / 5-minute grace).
